component.name: OxiTide
component.summary: High-resolution TIDAL player with bit-perfect playback

description.p: OxiTide is a native TIDAL desktop client for Linux, written entirely in Rust and built on GTK 4 / libadwaita. It streams Hi-Res and FLAC audio gaplessly and keeps the signal bit-perfect all the way to the output.

ul.li: Gapless Hi-Res / FLAC streaming with per-track sample-rate switching
Optional DSP chain: parametric EQ, convolution, tape and tube colour, stereo widener, limiter, resampler
Spectrum visualizer (bars, mirror, scope and more), live LUFS and dynamic-range meter
Synced lyrics drawer, queue drawer, Now Playing view
MPRIS media keys, Last.fm / ListenBrainz scrobbling, remote-control API

description.p: USB Rawlink (direct USB passthrough to a DAC) needs your user to be allowed to open the DAC's USB device. The native packages install a udev rule for that; in the Flatpak the app shows the one-line command to install the same rule on your system the first time it is needed.
A TIDAL subscription is required. OxiTide is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by TIDAL.

screenshot.caption: Home: custom mixes with the collapsed play bar
Top playlists, tracks, albums and artists
Hi-Res headphone classics and classic albums
Synced lyrics drawer with the full play bar and stream info

description.p: Cover grids fit the window, search results open collapsed, and the Tracks page gains Add to Playlist and queue actions. Your TIDAL profile picture shows as the avatar.
Add to Playlist now lists playlists inside folders, Check for Updates only offers Linux releases, and a new version takes over from one still running in the tray.
Playlists can now be created, edited and moved between folders from the Playlists page, and folders can be created there too.
Adding an album or track to a playlist works again, and the placeholder art for empty covers is back in every package.
The sidebar collapses to icons only with a toggle at the foot of the nav column, and the state is remembered across restarts.
The play bar no longer reaches across the sidebar, and its cover art is decoded at the display's real resolution instead of a fixed 80 pixels.

PipeWire is now the default output driver, so playback shares the system mixer; exclusive, bit-perfect output stays available through ALSA or USB Rawlink. The interface ships its own icon theme and renders the same on every desktop.

Fixed: no sound at all on a fresh install; memory growing by about a gigabyte a minute while browsing, caused by cover art decoded at full resolution and never released; liked tracks, albums and artists stopping at the first page; the tray icon staying invisible on KDE; and sign-in failing on systems without gst-plugins-good.

One-click USB authorization in the Flatpak build: the permission dialog installs the udev rule for you via a polkit password prompt and retries automatically. Fixed the output-device selection resetting to default (and playback staying silent) after authorizing a DAC.
Now-playing indicator on Home page track cards: the playing track's cover shows a live five-bar glyph.

Persistent per-DAC clock calibration with a learned-clocks table in settings. Fixed hardware-volume DACs playing quiet: the software volume stage is removed from the audio chain when the DAC's hardware volume is in control.
New app icon and store branding.
USB Rawlink: freshly plugged DACs are authorized reliably (udev rule ordering). Flatpak support with guided host udev-rule setup. Single USB authorization dialog.
First stable release: lyrics drawer, floating collapsible play bar with a stream-info display, instant pause/resume, visualizer modes incl. scope.
